newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Subsea quake shakes New Zealand's North Island.
newsitem.headline: Subsea quake shakes New Zealand's North Island.

text.p: An earthquake deep beneath remote islands in the Pacific shook much of New Zealand's North Island on Monday but initial reports indicated no damage.
The quake was also felt in eastern parts of South Island and railway operator TranzRail said it would check to ensure none of its rails had moved.
The Institute of Geological and Nuclear Science said it recorded a quake measuring 7.6 on the Richter scale centred on the Southern Kermadec Islands at 11.22 a.m. (2322 GMT Sunday).
The islands are about 900 km (540 miles)northeast of New Zealand's northern coastline.
The quake was at a depth of about 518 km (310 miles) and was probably too deep to cause much damage, an institute spokeswoman said.
